about.title: Long Beach Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Nineteen people lost their lives on Long Beach streets in 2025, according to public collision records. Behind each number is a Los Angeles County household trying to figure out what comes next — a shared mortgage, kids who need rides, a partner suddenly gone. A wrongful death claim exists for exactly that situation. It is a civil action, separate from any criminal case, and it asks the person or company responsible to answer for what the family has lost. Some of these losses trace to collisions on Atlantic Avenue, Long Beach Boulevard, Pacific Coast Highway or the I-405, though a claim can also follow a fall at a business, a defective product, or negligent care. Under California law the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children hold the first right to file, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The window is two years from the date of death, and shorter when a government entity is involved. LawProactive connects you, at no charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: What a Long Beach Family Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Not everyone can bring the claim
items.desc: California gives the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to sue, with certain dependents and heirs following. An attorney can sort out who in your family has standing before anything is filed.

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people expect
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death, but if a city, county or state agency is involved — say a Long Beach city vehicle or a poorly maintained public road — the deadline to give notice is much shorter.

items.title: The claim covers more than the funeral bill
items.desc: Recoverable losses include burial and funeral costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. None of that depends on whether a criminal case is filed.

items.question: The driver who caused the crash on the 405 in Long Beach is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and runs on its own track, separate from anything the Los Angeles County District Attorney decides to do. In fact, waiting can be risky, because the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of how long the criminal case takes. An attorney can coordinate the timing so evidence from one proceeding is not lost to the other.

items.question: My father wasn't married and I'm his adult child. Can I still file?
items.answer: Yes, in most cases. When there is no surviving spouse or domestic partner, the deceased person's children are next in line under California's wrongful death rules. If there were also no children, certain dependents or heirs may be able to step in. An attorney will review your family situation to confirm who qualifies.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect us with a lawyer?
items.answer: Nothing at all. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we do not take a cut of anything you recover. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
